title: Evaluating protein intake-induced feeding inhibition in Drosophila
author: Wang, Wang, et al.

steps.title: Assemble optogenetic and handling tools
steps.instruction: Build the light‑stimulus unit inside a 100 mm × 100 mm container that fits one fly bottle; wrap an LED strip (623 nm for activation, 533 nm for inhibition, size 110 cm × 10 mm) inside, connect to a power supply, turn on and adjust intensity with a digital optical laser power meter to 0.79 mW mm⁻² (623 nm) or 0.03 mW mm⁻² (533 nm). Prepare several aluminum‑foil sleeves for fly bottles and vials and a black‑cloth‑wrapped box to keep them dark. Construct a dispenser: a funnel whose inner diameter is slightly larger than the bottle outer diameter, a finger‑shaped tube (inner diameter slightly larger than the funnel’s narrow end, Ø × H = 18 mm × 95 mm) that connects to the funnel, and label a line for 100 flies (or a reference line for ~30 flies). Prepare the excretion test unit: 6 cm dishes with a 5 mm central lid hole, a 1 mL blue pipette tip cut to ~3 mm to fit the hole, a tunnel whose inner diameter is slightly larger than a fly vial (Ø × H = 23 mm × 95 mm), and seal the tip to the tunnel with Parafilm.

steps.title: Prepare normal fly food
steps.instruction: Cook 1 L Normal Food: weigh 68 g cornmeal, 16 g yeast, 9 g soybean powder, 5 g agar; add 1 L distilled water in an electric cooker, stir and bring to boil, maintain boiling for 30 min, then keep on “keep‑warm” until the mixture cools to 75 °C. Add 0.726 g anhydrous calcium chloride and 43 g maltose, stir 2–3 min until dissolved. Cool to 65 °C, add 5.0 mL propionic acid, stir 2–3 min. Pour ≈20 mL into each fly bottle, cover with sterilized double‑layer gauze, let solidify for ~3 h in a clean ventilated area. Store at 4 °C for ≤1 week.

steps.title: Prepare ATR‑supplemented food
steps.instruction: In darkness, make a 200 mM ATR stock by dissolving 1.0 g All‑Trans‑Retina in 17.578 mL anhydrous ethanol, vortex until clear. For opto‑activation, add 200 µL stock to 100 mL Normal Food kept at 60–65 °C (final 0.4 mM ATR). For opto‑inhibition, add 500 µL stock to 100 mL Normal Food (final 1 mM ATR). Stir thoroughly with a medicine spoon, then pour and store exactly as described for Normal Food (steps 2‑3).

steps.title: Prepare specialized assay foods
steps.instruction: Make 1 % agar starvation food (100 mL): add 1.0 g agar to 100 mL distilled water, stir, microwave until boiling, repeat boiling‑stir cycle three times to fully dissolve. Make 1.7 % tryptone pre‑feeding food (100 mL): add 1.7 g tryptone to 100 mL freshly boiled 1 % agar mix, stir until dissolved. Prepare feeding‑test foods with brilliant blue dye at 65 °C: for tryptone test, add 0.5 g brilliant blue to 100 mL 1.7 % tryptone; for Normal Food test, add 1.0 g brilliant blue to 100 mL Normal Food. Stir thoroughly. Pour into fly bottles or vials and store as in step 2. Use fully transparent containers (e.g., 100 mL glass beakers) for light‑stimulation steps.

steps.title: Cross and rear experimental flies
steps.instruction: Cross driver strains (Gal4 or LexA) with optogenetic responder lines (CsChrimson or GtACR). Label each bottle with a blind code assigned by a non‑experimenter. Rear flies on Normal Food at 25 °C, 40–60 % humidity, 12 h / 12 h light‑dark. When progeny eclose, remove all eclosed flies at day’s end and collect new eclosions every two days; mark the collection day as Day 2. Transfer flies to ATR‑containing Normal Food and age to Day 5: for opto‑inhibition, move to 1 mM ATR food on Day 2; for opto‑activation, keep on Normal Food for 2 days then switch to 0.4 mM ATR food on Day 4. Keep bottles wrapped in aluminum foil sleeves inside the black‑cloth box (complete darkness). Avoid CO₂ anesthesia; if used, allow ≥24 h recovery.

steps.title: Starve flies for 24 h
steps.instruction: In darkness (foil‑sleeved bottles inside black box), gently transfer all collected flies (same blind code) into a single agar bottle. Using the dispenser from step 1, split flies into groups of ~100 per agar bottle (or ~30 per vial) and label each bottle with the blind code. Starve the groups for 24 h at 25 °C, 40–60 % humidity.

steps.title: Warm food bottles before assay
steps.instruction: Remove food bottles from the refrigerator and let them reach room temperature for at least 3 h. Place ≈50–100 unanesthetized wild‑type flies into each bottle, let them remain for 30 min to saturate the food with fly odor, then carefully remove all flies.

steps.title: Conduct pre‑feeding treatment
steps.instruction: Gently transfer the starved flies into pre‑feeding bottles containing 1.7 % tryptone or 1 % agar (no blue dye). Press the bottle stopper down so the food surface is ~2 cm below the stopper, increasing fly‑food contact. Keep bottles in darkness at 25 °C, 40–60 % humidity for exactly 30 min (use a timer).

steps.title: Perform 10‑min feeding test
steps.instruction: Transfer pre‑fed flies into test bottles containing Normal Food with the appropriate blue dye. Press the stopper to position the food ~2 cm below the opening. Place each bottle into an optogenetic unit: use 623 nm light for activation, 533 nm for inhibition, or keep light OFF for control. Maintain 25 °C, 40–60 % humidity and allow feeding for exactly 10 min (timer). After 10 min, inspect the bottle wall for blue excretion dots. If dots are present, move flies to labeled empty vials and freeze both vials and the test bottle at –80 °C for ≥2 h (samples stable up to 2 weeks). If no dots, transfer flies to the excretion dishes (step 10). For ~100 flies, split them into three dishes (~30 flies each) using the finger‑shaped tube. To assess protein consumption directly, skip steps 8‑9 and transfer starved flies straight to 1.7 % tryptone food with blue dye (step 9).

steps.title: Execute excretion test
steps.instruction: Immediately after the feeding test, gently move flies into the excretion dishes through the 5 mm lid hole (section 1) and seal the hole with tape. Place dishes in optogenetic units with the same light condition as in step 9. Allow flies to excrete for 10 min (no vibration/noise), then freeze the dishes at –80 °C.

steps.title: Process samples for feeding assay
steps.instruction: Collect all flies (both sexes) into two 2 mL cryogenic vials (one per sex) labeled with the blind code. Remove vials from –80 °C, pour flies onto weighing paper, then re‑transfer each sex into a new labeled cryogenic vial. Submerge vials in liquid nitrogen, shake vigorously 7–8 times with a long tweezer to detach heads, legs, and wings. Pour the mixture through a 710 µm sieve; heads/legs/wings pass through, bodies remain on the sieve. Transfer bodies onto labeled weighing paper. Add one steel bead and 500 µL PBS to each Eppendorf grind tube. For ~100 flies, split bodies into three grind tubes of ~10 flies each; for ~30 flies, place all 10 flies in one tube. Grind at 60 Hz for 10 s, then centrifuge at 15 000 × g for 30 min. Pipette 100 µL supernatant from each tube into a 96‑well plate (for ~100 flies, one well per tube; for ~30 flies, load each tube three times as technical replicates). Include three PBS blanks. Measure absorbance at 620 nm with a plate reader and record the values.

steps.title: Process samples for excretion assay
steps.instruction: For test bottles that showed blue dots, wash the dots with PBS and measure absorbance as described in the original study. For excretion dishes, retrieve dishes from –80 °C, pour flies onto weighing paper, count N flies, and collect flies into a 2 mL cryogenic vial. Process these flies exactly as in step 11 (heads removal, grinding, centrifugation). Rinse each dish repeatedly with 1.5 mL PBS until all visible blue dots dissolve. Pipette 100 µL of the rinse liquid into a well of a 96‑well plate, repeating three times per dish. Measure absorbance at 620 nm.

steps.title: Analyze absorbance data
steps.instruction: Export all plate‑reader readings. Compute “Average PBS” from the three PBS blanks. For each sample, calculate Food Consumption (FC): average the three sample repeats, then subtract Average PBS (FCAgar = mean – Average PBS for agar groups; FCTryptone = mean – Average PBS for tryptone groups). Average the FCAgar values of maternal‑control groups to obtain Average(FC Maternal Control). Compute Relative Food Consumption (RFC) for each sample as FC / Average(FC Maternal Control). For tryptone groups, calculate Suppression Index (SI): SI = (RFCTryptone – Average RFCAgar) / Average RFCAgar. Also compute Relative Excretion (REX): adjust excretion values by dividing by N flies and multiplying by 30, then normalize to Average(FC Maternal Control). Compute Excretion‑to‑Retention Ratio (ERR): ERR = Excretion / average FC (separately for agar and tryptone). Perform statistical analysis in GraphPad Prism: mean ± SEM, Student’s t‑test for two groups, one‑way ANOVA with Dunnett’s post‑test for multiple groups, two‑way ANOVA for interaction effects. Significance: * p < 0.05, ** p < 0.01, *** p < 0.001.
